title: Sojourner Truth gave a speech that never included the phrase “Ain't I a Woman”
summary: On this day in 1851, abolitionist and women's right activist Sojourner Truth gave her most famous speech to the Ohio Women's Rights Convention in Akron, Ohio. Subsequently published in the abolitionist newspaper The Anti-Slavery Bugle in June 1851, the speech has become known as the “Ain't I a Woman?” speech, although it did not include that phrase. That iconic line was added to Truth's speech (along with a Southern dialect that Truth, as a Dutch-speaking New Yorker, certainly did not have) in an 1863 publication, likely as a well-intentioned literary device for propaganda purposes.
